The Avengers ventured to the hazardous area, or the "red zone", to find the cause of the attack.[559] To their horror, they learned that a U.S. government facility was behind the bio-weapon.[560] In a fight with A.I.M. agents, She-Hulk was contaminated and went savage after being exposed to Jack of Hearts' radioactive powers.[561] While the Avengers battled an enraged She-Hulk, Iron Man and Black Panther were kept under arrest in the Pentagon. Rusk revealed himself to be the Red Skull after attacking the Falcon and Gyrich.[562] Despite defeating Captain America and nearly killing the Falcon, the Black Panther managed to knock him out with Falcon's assistance. The Avengers were able to disperse an antidote for the infection and prevent more deaths. However, the savage She-Hulk was still missing.[563]

Afraid of what was happening to her, She-Hulk had gone to look for her cousin, the original Hulk. The Avengers, joined by Hawkeye, tracked She-Hulk down, causing her to uncontrollably attack them.[564] She-Hulk's rampage led to the destruction of the small town where Bruce Banner had been hiding.[565] Banner attempted to reason with She-Hulk, but when the military arrived, Hawkeye shot him with an arrow to provoke his transformation, hoping the two Hulks would keep each other busy, rather than killing the soldiers.[566] The two Hulks were ultimately defeated by Jack of Hearts, who managed to restore She-Hulk's reasoning with his volatile powers.[567]

With doubts as to whether or not Jack and She-Hulk could coexist on the team, the Avengers reached a decision for Jack to take a leave of absence. Soon after, Jack sacrificed himself to save Ant-Man's daughter from a kidnapper, ending the long feud the two Avengers had experienced during their tenure.[568]

During an attempted robbery in England, an innocent and heroic mother, Kelsey Leigh, became a casualty as the Avengers tussled against the Wrecking Crew.[569] Chosen by the previous Captain Britain Brian Braddock, she was reborn as the new Captain Britain, wielding the Sword of Might. Captain Britain and the Avengers fought the Wrecking Crew after they brutally maimed Hawkeye.[570] The intriguer manipulating the Wrecking Crew was revealed to be Morgan Le Fay, who had captured and tortured Brian Braddock, seized control of Avalon and wished to destroy Captain Britain in order to ravage England. Ultimately, Leigh managed to overpower Morgan alongside the Avengers, joining their ranks as Captain Britain.[571] Soon after, the New Invaders led by U.S.Agent carried out a plot to depose the government of Mazikhandar,[572] recruiting Namor to their cause.[573] The Avengers clashed with them over their reckless and illegal plan,[574] but failed to stop Namor and the Atlantean army from securing victory.[575]

Avengers Disassembled[]

The Avengers endured their worst days as a series of tragic events befell the team. During a United Nations' conference, Tony Stark went on a hateful tirade showing unexplainably signs of drunkenness. Simultaneously, an undead Jack of Hearts happened upon the mansion grounds and self-detonated, murdering Ant-Man and partially destroying the building. This was followed by a Quinjet piloted by the Vision utterly destroying the Mansion. The Vision claimed the team had failed in their purpose and spew out an army of Ultron drones to punish his teammates. During the attack, She-Hulk went on a rampage, destroyed the Vision and brutally assaulted the Avengers, beating the Wasp and Captain Britain into comas.[576] Stark, who had now lost his political office as the Secretary of Defense, managed to knock She-Hulk out and place her under S.H.I.E.L.D.'s arrest, giving the Avengers time to recover themselves.[577]

All former Avengers available responded to the crisis at the ruins of the Avengers Mansion, just as United Nations declared they had severed their ties with the team. Unexpectedly, the heroes were attacked by a Kree armada in a battle that cost Hawkeye his life.[578] As the Kree vanished, Doctor Strange arrived on the scene claiming that magic was being abused. The Avengers realized that the mastermind behind the attacks was the Scarlet Witch. The return of repressed memories of the loss of her children combined with her rapidly growing powers caused a nervous breakdown and the loss of her grasp on reality. Strange led the Avengers to the Scarlet Witch in Whisper Hill and a fight broke out. Subdued by the Eye of Agamotto, the Scarlet Witch was defeated and surrendered to Magneto in order to being put under the care of Professor Xavier.[579] Tony Stark gathered the active Avengers to a final meeting, announcing he no longer had the financial means to keep sponsoring the team. One by one, each of the Avengers declared their intentions to leave the team, being shaken by the trauma of the Scarlet Witch's attack, as well as other losses, such as the disappearance of Thor and Asgard. The damaged Mansion was turned into a memorial site. After sharing their fondest memories of the Avengers, the team disassembled.[580]

Earth's Mightiest Heroes were reassembled by fate and were made official the efforts of Iron Man and Captain America, who formed the New Avengers with the primary purpose of recapturing the numerous super-powered criminals that had escaped the maximum-security penitentiary known as the Raft. The reformed group was no longer attached to a charter or regulated by governmental institutions.[581] Also, when Iron Lad, a teenage version of Kang, recruited teenage individuals with ties to the Avengers to face his future self, the Young Avengers carried on their inspirational idols' legacy.[582]

An ideological schism became the cause of the new Avengers' dispersal. The passage of the Superhuman Registration Act split the superhuman community in half, with one side being led by Iron Man in registering with the authorities and enforcing security while the other was led by Captain America in rebelling against the new law and fighting for personal liberty. In a superhuman civil war, Iron Man's Initiative emerged victorious over Captain America's outlawed Avengers.[583] Named the new director of S.H.I.E.L.D., Iron Man commanded the registered super heroes, assembling a mighty team of Avengers,[584] while Luke Cage resisted with a small group of remaining rebels to fight as pariahs in honor of Captain America after his public assassination.[585]

The Initiative was profoundly compromised by Skrulls in the wake of their alien Secret Invasion. With Starktech heavily hacked, Iron Man was largely blamed for allowing the infiltration to happen, which led to his ousting as director of S.H.I.E.L.D.. Responsible for executing the Skrull queen, Norman Osborn, Spider-Man's former archenemy Green Goblin, was publicly acclaimed and made the new head of national security.[586] Supplanting S.H.I.E.L.D. with H.A.M.M.E.R., Osborn assembled a dark formation of Avengers consisting of former super villains posing as heroes and became an opposition to the former Avengers, who were forced to survive out of the law.[587] During Osborn's rule, Hank Pym became the leader of a group of peculiar Avengers who were secretly guided by Loki,[588] while former agents of the Initiative left the program to create the Avengers Resistance as a revival of the New Warriors.[589]

Osborn descended into lunacy due to Loki's machinations and decided to launch a siege to Asgard, in Broxton. Thor initially resisted Osborn, his Avengers, H.A.M.M.E.R. and the Initiative by himself until a resurrected Captain America assembled an army of heroes to protect the magic city and oppose the invasion. However, one of Osborn's Avengers, the mad Sentry, represented an unexpected danger to all involved as he obliterated Asgard. Empowering all who fought on Asgard's side with the Norn Stones, Loki was killed by the Sentry; his sacrifice allowed the Avengers to finally end the dark Avenger.[590] Following Osborn's defeat, Captain America, Iron Man and Thor settled their differences in an adventure across the Nine Realms to stop the powerful Hela wielding the Twilight Sword.[591] In the aftermath, Osborn and most of his Avengers were taken into custody. Captain America was tasked with being the new head of security for superhuman affairs as Commander Steve Rogers under the condition of the Registration Act being thrown out.[592]

Heroic Age[]

The Avengers were reassembled as free and independent heroes. Commander Steve Rogers recruited Iron Man, Thor, Hawkeye, Spider-Woman, Spider-Man, Wolverine and Bucky, the new Captain America, to operate at the Avengers Tower as part of a team run by former S.H.I.E.L.D. director Maria Hill.[593] In addition to this, Luke Cage had his team formalized as the New Avengers based at the Avengers Mansion,[594] Rogers also led a covert operation of Secret Avengers,[595] and Hank Pym and a team of former Avengers became trainers at the Avengers Academy.[596]

The recently reassembled Avengers were contacted by Kang the Conqueror, who alerted them that in the future Ultron would be able to establish a ruthless and artificial empire. The children of the Avengers would oppose his rule but threaten the fabric of reality by doing so.[593] In need of a time machine, the Avengers were advised by Wolverine to recruit the Kree interdimensional expeditioner Noh-Varr. In their research, the Avengers learned the timestream was damaged.[597] Momentarily attacked by Horsemen of Apocalypse from another timeline, the Avengers decided to travel to the apocalyptic future to heal the timestream.[598] In the future, some of the Avengers witnessed a brutal war against Ultron with the resistance being led by Iron Man and Bruce Banner as Kang's allies, while in the present the rest of the team were joined by Killraven as transtemporal threats invaded Earth.[599] The break in reality was caused by Kang's trips and threw the Avengers in a time loop.[600] They contacted Ultron instead, asking him to preserve space time by surrendering to Kang; Ultron let Kang and his army of Avengers destroy him. The Avengers returned to the present and Iron Man started to prepare himself for Ultron's upcoming rise.[601]

In a greedy quest for power, the villainous Hood secured some of the Infinity Stones from their curators, the Illuminati. He crossed paths with the Red Hulk, who, being violently beaten, approached the Avengers Tower for help.[602] Iron Man had the Illuminati investigate by themselves, but the secret cabal's secret existence was discovered by Commander Rogers and the Avengers, much to their anger.[603] In an uneasy team-up, they sought for reassembling the Infinity Gauntlet to detain the Hood.[604] Managing to wield the Gauntlet, Iron Man resisted the omnipotent temptation to use the it to create an utopia. After teleporting the Hood back to prison and the Infinity Gauntlet away, Iron Man pretended to have destroyed the latter and disbanded the Illuminati. In reality, the Illuminati redistributed the Infinity Stones again, with Steve Rogers joining their ranks this time.[605]

In between these adventures, Wonder Man publicly opposed the reformation of the Avengers due to the past tragedies they had inflicted, arguing they caused more harm than good.[593] His attempts to dissuade Steve Rogers went to the extremes of attacking the Avengers,[597] and being unconvinced of letting them exist.[602] Having assembled the Revengers, he outpowered Luke Cage's team and moved his attack to the Avengers Tower.[606] He publicly exposed the Avengers as a violent and risky project. Though captured alongside the Revengers in the end, Wonder Man was able to furtively escape after making the public be wary of Earth's Mightiest Heroes.[607]

Fear Itself & Shattered Heroes[]

When the Asgardian god of fear, the deadly Serpent, resurfaced with the help of the Red Skull's daughter Sin, a group of super humans was empowered by magical hammers similar to Mjolnir. As the Worthy, they spread fear around the world to venerate their master in his plans of becoming the All-Father of Asgard. Reclaiming his position as the ruler of Asgard, Odin retreated and let the mortals to fend for themselves.[608] A corrupted Thing caused the Avengers Tower to fall in a deadly combat against the Red Hulk.[609] Moreover, as one of the Serpent's generals, Sin stormed Washington, D.C., with a Nazi army, causing Captain America's apparent death, which prompted Steve Rogers to step back as the star-spangled soldier.[610] All over the globe, the Avengers kept resisting the destructive Worthy.[611] Iron Man briefly sacrificed his sobriety to provoke Odin and have access to the Asgardian forges. Wielding Uru weapons manufactured by Iron Man in the furnaces of Nidavellir, many Avengers were empowered as the Mighty to oppose the Serpent's army. Thor bravely slayed the Serpent at the ultimate cost of his own life. The war-torn Avengers had a hard work to rebuild the world ahead of themselves but were able to do it without fear.[612] The Mighty Thor would eventually make a journey back to the living.[613]

The shattered team temporarily relocated to the Avengers Mansion with the destruction of the Avengers Tower.[614] As Osborn escaped prison and rebuilt H.A.M.M.E.R. by allying himself with Madame Hydra's Hydra, Monica Rappaccini's A.I.M. and the Gorgon's Hand,[615] Captain America formed a new team with Iron Man, Hawkeye, Spider-Woman, Noh-Varr, the X-Man and Queen of Wakanda Storm, the rebuilt Vision and S.H.I.E.L.D. super-agent Quake. During the new group's first press release, they were attacked in the media by Osborn by being labelled as authoritarian figures.[616] The Avengers divided their forces to tackle potential H.A.M.M.E.R. bases. However, Iron Man's armor was hacked and Captain America was kidnapped.[617] With the Avengers overpowered, Osborn managed to gain public and governmental support[618] to sanction H.A.M.M.E.R. back to power.[619] In a final confrontation against the Avengers however, Osborn was a victim of his own lust for power. Having been turned into a Super-Adaptoid, he collapsed due to the strain of the alterations. H.A.M.M.E.R. was no more and the Avengers regained their credibility. Madame Hydra took the opportunity to strengthen Hydra by recruiting power.[620] Some time later, she had Hydra combine Super-Adaptoid technology with Mandroid units. In Madripoor, the original Avengers coincidentally met each other while secretly investigating her operations. As a battle ensued, several other members of the Avengers answered the distress call for the mission to stop Hydra.[621]

The Avengers Tower was rebuilt and the Avengers faced the new iteration of the Zodiac, who attempted to amass the vast array of cosmic-level weapons found in the planet.[622] The Avengers were joined by the Hulk, who had previously clashed with the villains.[623] It was revealed that Thanos had outfitted the Zodiac to act as his agents in his quest for ultimate power.[624] The Avengers were offered help by Thanos' adversaries, the Guardians of the Galaxy and marched to space to defeat the Mad Titan.[625] Though the deadly villain empowered himself with a Cosmic Cube replica,[626] he was ultimately defeated by the cojoined efforts of the Avengers, the Guardians and the Elders of the Universe, who had been recruited by Thor.[627]

The Children's Crusade[]

The fate of the Scarlet Witch still haunted the Avengers. Having been missing since the M-Day, when she unreasonably wiped most of the mutant population after reshaping reality,[628] she became the main interest of the Young Avengers, who went on a quest to find her, something the Avengers opposed to. Young Avengers members Wiccan and Speed were supposedly her missing children, which led Magneto to join them in their mission.[629] The amnesiac Scarlet Witch was found in Latveria under Doctor Doom's influence. The Avengers joined Wonder Man in order to prevent the Young Avengers from causing problems.[630] The Scarlet Witch and the Young Avengers were rescued by Iron Lad, in a process which led Ant-Man to deceive death and the Scarlet Witch's memories to resurface.[631]

Resuming her attack against the Avengers, the Scarlet Witch only ceased it upon learning about Wiccan's and Speed's existence. Her return was met with caution by the X-Men, who had been severely harmed by her past actions and wished to apprehend her.[632] Avengers and X-Men battled for the Scarlet Witch's freedom. She teleported away with the Young Avengers and sought assistance from Doctor Doom in restoring mutantkind. However, Doom cunningly seized her and Wiccan's powers for his own interests.[633] Avengers and X-Men battled the all-powerful Doctor Doom, whose powers backfired at him with the actions of the Scarlet Witch and Wiccan, though at the cost of Ant-Man's daughter Cassie Lang, the Young Avenger Stature.[634] The Scarlet Witch was back with a long journey of redemption ahead of herself.[635]

Avengers vs. X-Men[]

A subsequent mutant-related crisis came in the form of mutant terrorist Cable, who had previously sacrificed himself to ensure his daughter Hope's survival. As the first mutant born after M-Day, Hope was prophesied to restore the mutant race.[636] Upon his return from the future, the terminal Cable targeted the Avengers, knowing they could be a danger for Hope. During a fight against Grim Reaper and the Lethal Legion, the Avengers were secretly attacked by Cable, who captured Falcon, Captain America and Iron Man, but found in the Red Hulk a challenging opponent.[637] The Avengers were unexpectedly assisted by Hope and the X-Men's leader Cyclops.[638] With the Avengers freed, Cable was overpowered and fell. Avengers and X-Men parted ways in a tense but also amicable way.[639]

Matters escalated when the Avengers learned through the young space hero Nova that the all-consuming Phoenix was coming to Earth. In a secret mission, some Avengers attempted to intercept the Phoenix in outer space. Meanwhile, the Avengers assembled an army to contact the X-Men on their island base Utopia to hand over Hope, who was prophesied to ascend as the new Phoenix to restore mutantkind.[640] Storm left the Avengers in protest, allying herself with her long-time mutant teammates.[641] The X-Men's disagreement with the Avengers sparked a battle. Hope took the opportunity to decide her own destiny and escaped.[642] The X-Men tricked the Avengers, feigning surrender to actually look for Hope. With Wolverine sharing the possibility of slaying Hope, Captain America chose to evict him from the mission to track her. Scattering her signal, Hope led Avengers and X-Men clash in different misguided locations, namely Wakanda, Tabula Rasa, Latveria, Mount Wundagore and the Savage Land. Hope approached Wolverine by herself, seeking help in preventing the Phoenix in their own way by going to the Blue Area of the Moon to divert the cosmic bird entity from Earth.[643]

On space, the Avengers unsuccessfully attempted to destroy the Phoenix.[644] During the mission, Noh-Varr was secretly tasked by the Kree Supreme Intelligence of containing its power instead. Divided, Noh-Varr betrayed the Avengers in the Kree Galaxy.[645] Although he regretted his decision and rebelled against the Intelligence, he gained the Avengers' mistrust, being exiled both from Earth and Hala.[646] On the Moon, the Avengers were alerted by Wolverine about Hope's location, attracting the X-Men.[643] With a badly injured Thor crashing onto the Moon, the Phoenix's coming was announced. Avengers and X-Men descended into a brawl as the power of the Phoenix increased within Hope and she found herself unable to control it. Desperate, she asked Wolverine to end her, although Cyclops prevented him from doing so. Iron Man used a special armor to try to destroy the Phoenix, but he only managed to splinter it, causing it to take the five X-Men present as hosts: namely Cyclops, Emma Frost, Namor, Colossus and Magik.[647]

The five Phoenixes returned to Utopia, uniting mutantkind and providing resources and executing actions to improve the world, rendering the Avengers obsolete as a peacemaking force.[648] Unsatisfied with the potential of the Phoenix for evil, the Avengers continued to be an opposing force, even sending the Red Hulk to end their threat for good.[649] In an attempt to rescue Hope from Utopia, the Avengers were successful in their mission due to the Scarlet Witch's intervention.[648] Such aggression represented an act of war, with the X-Men turning their attention into incapacitating the Avengers by shutting down their operations and capturing many of their members. When the Avengers captured the mutant Transonic during a conflict between the X-Men and the Scarlet Witch, Namor was convinced by Emma Frost to attack the Avengers in their current base, Wakanda.[650] Namor and his Atlantean army flooded Wakanda, and some Avengers escaped to K'un-Lun with Hope. The Avengers narrowly managed to defeat Namor, at the cost of great damage to themselves and Wakanda. With Namor defeated, his portion of the Phoenix Force was bequeathed to the other four hosts.[651]

With their power amplified, the Phoenixes acted erratically and showed signs of losing control. Moreover, with the fall of Wakanda, Storm's marriage to Black Panther was annulled. These events led the X-Men to question the integrity of the Phoenix and many of their members abandoned Utopia. As the Avengers staged a prison breakout for their fellows, Colossus and Magik lost their portions of the Phoenix after being manipulated by Spider-Man.[652] In K'un-Lun, Cyclops tried to recapture Hope, but was fended off by Shou-Lao and Hope herself, who managed to nullify his powers and teleport him away to the Moon.[653] Iron Man studied ways to counter the Phoenix with the Scarlet Witch's and Hope's powers.[654] Several X-Men teamed up with the Avengers, who were also joined by the Hulk. Together, they attacked Cyclops and Frost and gained the upper hand until Cyclops took the final piece of the Phoenix from Frost, making him the sole host as Dark Phoenix upon which he killed Professor X, who had attempted to stop him.[655] Avengers and X-Men combated the destruction the Phoenix produced around Earth. He was exorcized of the maddening power by the Scarlet Witch and Hope. Using the Phoenix's powers, Hope restored the devastation caused by Cyclops. Alongside the Scarlet Witch, she decided to dissipate the Phoenix Force, which caused new mutants to manifest all over the world since the M-Day. Cyclops was incarcerated.[656]

Acknowledging the Avengers should have been more actively involved with mutantkind's struggles instead of standing by while the world hated them, Captain America wished to rectify this negligence by forming the Avengers Unity Squad, a team of Avengers led by Cyclops' brother, Havok, in hopes of keeping Charles Xavier's dream of coexistence between mutants and humans alive.[657]

Age of Ultron[]

The Avengers resumed their operations in the aftermath of their war against the Phoenix. They interrupted Mister Negative's criminal activities following Madame Hydra's tip.[658] Next, they were unexpectedly contacted by a former member who was trapped in the Microverse.[659] During the Skrull Invasion, the Wasp had apparently perished due to the aliens' attack.[660] In fact, she had struggled to survive in Microverse for a long time. Being met by the original Avengers following her call for help, the Wasp joined them to resist the ruthless Lord Gouzar.[661] The group was assisted by Wonder Man, who regretted his previous attacks and wished to make up for them. The Wasp was rescued by the Avengers, and they were followed by Lord Gouzar. In an epic battle, the Avengers fended off the villain and forced him back to the microscopic plane of existence.[662]

Ultron's attack turned out to take place in a way more violent way than expected. His drones obliterated the civilized world, and the Avengers were forced to hide in face of many heroes being executed. A small resistance was led by Iron Man as a hopeless Captain America was unable to inspire the heroes in the devastated world.[663] Coming up with a plan, Captain America led a strike against the artificial intelligence and the Avengers learned that Ultron attacked Earth from the future via the Vision. Out of time, Ultron was invincible.[664] The Avengers escaped to the Savage Land, where they met Nick Fury with Black Widow's assistance, being able to travel to the future to stop Ultron.[665] In the future, Ultron's power was absolute and the heroes had no chance against his forces, being utterly terminated.[666]

Wolverine and the Invisible Woman had a secret alternative plan of themselves of traveling to the past instead. To prevent Ultron's rise to power, they killed Hank Pym before he could ever create the killing machine. The results were devastating, in a world without Pym, the Avengers disbanded, Earth's Mightiest Heroes were the Defenders led by Commander America, Iron Man was a gloomy and authoritarian cyborg and magics had an extreme influence in the world under Morgan Le Fay's rule.[667] Terrified of this alternate possibility, Wolverine and Invisible Woman traveled back one more time, this time to ensure Ultron's creation. This time, they instructed Pym to install a hidden failsafe code to prevent Ultron from reaching absolute power. Just before the war against the Serpent, Ultron was activated by the super villain genius from Intelligencia, fighting the Avengers upon awakening. Unable to escape and deactivated by Pym's code, he never succeeded, but the timestream was severely damaged by the heroes' aggressions to it.[668] Moreover, the program that incapacitated Ultron devolved into a malicious cybernetic entity, prompting Pym and the Vision to establish an A.I. specialized Avengers squad.[669]

Avengers Machine[]

In Wakanda, Black Panther discovered dangerous multiversal phenomena known as incursions, which caused the collision between planets Earth of two different realities, extinguishing their respective universes. To prevent the catastrophic effect, either of the planets should be destroyed to stop the crash. Black Panther reunited the Illuminati to discuss solutions for the crisis.[670] The Illuminati reluctantly acknowledged the inevitability of destroying alternate worlds to preserve Earth. Captain America rejected this notion, heroically suggesting the Infinity Gauntlet as an alternative.[671] During an incursion, Captain America managed to prevent Earth's destruction with the Gauntlet, but the artifact broke down outside its native reality. The desperate Illuminati agreed to wipe from his memory his knowledge about their secret cabal, as well as any knowledge of incursions, in order to darkly protect the world in secrecy.[672]

Under the pretense the Avengers needed reshaping, Iron Man presented Captain America with a chart to expand its roster: the Avengers Machine.[673] In reality, Iron Man sought a powerful team to handle any overt threat while the Illuminati focused on solving the incursions.[674] The Avengers Machine was implemented when Earth's Mightiest Heroes Captain America, Iron Man, Thor, Black Widow, Hawkeye and the Hulk responded to the terraformation of an area in Mars. The evolutionary mechanisms known as Ex Nihilo and Abyss wished to transform Earth from their Garden as an experiment. The Avengers were unable to stop them, being captured. Captain America was sent back to Earth as a message to the world. Upon his recovery he went to his team's rescue, with his recruits being Carol Danvers as Captain Marvel, Falcon, Spider-Woman (Jessica Drew), Spider-Man (Peter Parker), Wolverine, master of kung fu Shang-Chi, universal teleporter Manifold, mutants Sunspot and Cannonball, Shi'ar Imperial Guardswoman Smasher, incursion survivor and supreme super hero Hyperion, and the embodiment of creation Captain Universe.[673]

The Avengers' mightiest team ever confronted the mad interlopers as they attempted to make Earth itself alive by installing evolutionary systems in different locations. Out of respect for the image of Captain Universe, Ex Nihilo and Abyss agreed to stop tampering with Earth, secluding themselves in their Martian Garden.[675] Their systems, however, kept being an interest to the Avengers. As a result of a White Event, one of Ex Nihilo's creations ascended as the Nightmask while a college student named Kevin Connor became the Starbrand in a catastrophic awakening.[676] Confronted by the Avengers, they approached Ex Nihilo and Abyss, but ultimately surrendered upon realizing the immense destruction they had been causing on Earth.[677] In Regina, the Avengers assessed a situation in which another system caused the destruction of Omega Flight.[678]

Meanwhile, the Avengers found that A.I.M. was especially interested in upcoming events related to the fate of Earth. On the Savage Land, the team witnessed as the mad scientists tampered with the birth of Ex Nihilo's Children of the Sun, managing to protect the living beings.[679] They were also targeted by the High Evolutionary, who wished to evaluate the Children of the Sun's potential in reawakening Terminus. Helped by Garokk the Petrified Man, the Avengers stopped the Evolutionary.[680] Simultaneously, the Avengers also learned A.I.M. had been expanding their power and resources as an army.[681] This was made evident when Ex Nihilo's systems started to cause more frequent calamities around the world. On A.I.M. Island, a powerful system was activated by A.I.M.'s minister Superia in the form of planetary defensive android.[682] The Avengers were brutally beaten by the mysterious mechanism, which was trapped by Superia. Manifold was ultimately able to scatter A.I.M.'s forces.[683] Simultaneously, S.H.I.E.L.D. had also been dealing with A.I.M.'s expansion with their own operation of Secret Avengers.[684]

In between the crises concerning these planetary systems, the Avengers dealt with more domestic affairs. They intervened in Slorenian politics one more time as its democracy was threatened by the actions of surviving nazis who had secretly weaponized the Asgardian beast Nidhogg to manipulate the future of the war-torn country.[685] Moreover, the Machine lost members. Spider-Man was secretly possessed by his former enemy Doctor Octopus, who worked with the Avengers as the Superior Spider-Man.[686] His erratic and obnoxious behavior ultimately led the impostor to sever ties with the group.[687] Wolverine lost his healing factor, becoming a liability[688] and ultimately being vulnerable to death.[689]

A broken Captain Universe alerted Manifold about an upcoming threat that had set course to Earth in the form of the Builders, a powerful ancient species who had the objective of destroying the planet that was the focal point of the incursions.[690] As they razed planets on their path, Manifold suggested that the Avengers Machine should include Ex Nihilo, Abyss, Nightmask and Starbrand to be able to fend off the raiders.[683] As most major alien empires in the Galactic Council suffered at the Builders' hands, the Avengers, guided by S.W.O.R.D., forged an intergalactic alliance to stop the Builders' deadly journey.[691]

Captain America and Captain Marvel difficultly led the Avengers to fight the Builders alongside Skrulls, the Kree, the Shi'ar, the Spartax, the Annihilation Wave and the Brood in an attempt to trap the enemies in a singularity at the Corridor. Their plan unexpectedly failed due to the Builders' enormous fleet. The Avengers were divided by the attack, with Captain Marvel's team being lost and apprehended by the Builders, who were intrigued by the Avengers having so many peculiar resources. Facing opposition, the Builders employed other Ex Nihilii to decay worlds, leaving the Avengers and the Galactic Council to tend for uncountable refugees.[692]

When the Spartoi emperor J'son attempted to defect to save himself from the Builders' ire,[693] the brutal aliens retaliated by pinpointing his location and ravaging their refuge. Many alien empires, including the Kree, surrendered to the Builders, who shared that Earth was their main target. Liberating Captain Marvel's team, the Avengers counted with the powerful Starbrand to counter the Builders armada. Meanwhile, the Avengers Ex Nihilo and Abyss managed to recruit the Builders' Ex Nihilii to their cause as their original purpose was to create life instead of ending it.[694] The Avengers feigned surrender, allowing Thor to liberate Hala from the Builders by slaying one of their agents.[695] However, their forces were still adamant and the Shi'ar momentarily retreated. The Ex Nihilii were able to summon Captain Universe, who was able to easily eliminate the Builders.[696] The universe recognized the merit of the Avengers in the war for liberating worlds at peril.[697]

At the same time, Thanos learned that the Illuminati used to own the Infinity Stones. As Earth had no Avengers, it was vulnerable to him and to his death generals of the Black Order.[691] To resist one of Thanos' agents Proxima Midnight, Luke Cage formed a mighty group of Avengers to battle her.[698] Meanwhile, the Illuminati learned that Thanos had a secret objective which was executing an abomination he had birthed in the form of an Inhuman son.[699] The Inhuman king Black Bolt detonated Attilan with a Terrigen Bomb in a useless attack against Thanos.[694] The explosion liberated Terrigen Mists in the atmosphere, triggering the activation of the Inhuman gene in Thanos' lost son Thane in the hidden city of Orollan,[695] but he was eventually found and captured by Thanos. Upon learning that Thanos stormed Earth,[697] the Avengers returned home with their grateful allies. On Earth's orbit, Thanos' armada was exterminated,[700] in Orollan, the Avengers themselves stroke at Thanos. In the end, Thane vanished after trapping Thanos in a living death state with his powers, and the Illuminati took custody of the Mad Titan. Earth was saved and it was proven to be an Avengers world.[701]

In the aftermath of the Builder war, the Avengers were visited by the Iron Man of Year 3030, who informed them about a rogue planet that would collide with Earth. With her help, the Avengers managed to phase the rogue planet into Earth, the Avengers World. This granted the Avengers an extra weaponized resource for difficult times to come, and Iron Man 3030 went back to her time.[702] Moreover, the Terrigen in the atmosphere triggered several incidents related to newly activated Inhumans. The Avengers addressed some of these crises, such as when Spider-Girl teamed up with them to interrupt Toxic Doxie from her vile experimentations on vulnerable Inhumans.[703]

Avengers World[]

The Avengers also fully cooperated with S.H.I.E.L.D., dealing with simultaneous crises all over the world at the same time.[704] On A.I.M. Island, they witnessed the expansion of the terrorist scientists' empire, with Smasher being mentally controlled by them.[705] Meanwhile, the Avengers fought the Gorgon and the Hand, who had taken control of the island nation of Madripoor. In a deadly fight, Shang-Chi apparently perished against the Gorgon.[706] In Italy, the group was joined by S.H.I.E.L.D. agent Druid and stumbled upon a subterranean city of undead zombies ruled by Morgan Le Fay.[707]

Oriented by the Hulk and herded by Manifold, the Avengers organized themselves to combat the multiple threats by joining forces with a multitude of allies.[708] Falcon found Shang-Chi safe with S.P.E.A.R., the Eastern version of S.H.I.E.L.D.. He joined their group, the Ascendants, to combat the Gorgon.[709] In Italy, the Avengers were assisted by Black Knight and the Euroforce against Morgan as she ravaged Europe.[710] Meanwhile, Sunspot and Cannonball traveled to the future where Ultron battled Kang to recruit Jocasta and the Avengers' children in order to seige A.I.M. Island.[711] Striking at different points, the Avengers assembled and defeated all of their enemies for the whole world had embraced their mission.[712]

The alliance between the Avengers and S.H.I.E.L.D. also came in hand when alternate versions of the original Avengers interloped on Earth. Earth's Mightiest Villains had been saved from an incursion by being interdimensionally retrieved by A.I.M., who sent Adaptoids to collect the fugitives in a brutal fight. Maria Hill and S.H.I.E.L.D. came upon the corpse of their Ant-Man and contacted the Avengers to investigate. Meanwhile, Bruce Banner met his rogue duplicate and replaced him.[713] As the two Avengers groups fought each other, A.I.M. intervened as to eliminate any hints of their involvement by recapturing the invaders and banishing them to another dimension.[714] On A.I.M. Island, the Hulk learned about the incursions and the premature death of the multiverse. He also realized that Iron Man and the Illuminati were probably reformed and dealing with the crisis secretly. In the end, the Hulk faked his own arrest and joined the Illuminati.[674]

Following an exposure to the dead Watcher's eye, which revealed deep secrets in its blast radius,[715] Captain America's memories about the Illuminati and the incursions eventually resurfaced, prompting him to direct the Avengers Machine against Tony Stark. Upon confronting his ally, friend, rival and enemy, Captain America and a group of Avengers were unexpectedly drafted across time by the Time Stone from the broken Infinity Gauntlet.[716] In their infinite journey, Captain America and the Avengers interacted with several developments of the Avengers.[717] Captain America was ultimately retrieved by Iron Lad, Kang and Immortus, who were, together, the last Avenger. They attempted to convince the star-spangled hero not to oppose Iron Man and the Illuminati. In the end, influenced by a future version of Hawkeye, Captain America confronted the time travelers and returned to the past, deciding to start a war against the Illuminati.[718]

AXIS[]

Much changed for the Avengers and the Illuminati in the meantime. Captain America had the source of his powers and youth neutralized by the villain Iron Nail,[719] with Sam Wilson, the former Falcon, assuming the Captain America mantle.[720] Moreover, Thor lost his sense of worthiness as an attack by Nick Fury, being unable to wield Mjolnir anymore.[721] After this, the Red Skull, who had been empowered by the telepathic brain of Charles Xavier,[722] established mutant concentration camps on Genosha. Finding resistance in the Avengers Unity Squad and in Magneto,[723] the Nazi villain ascended as the Red Onslaught and spread a telepathic hate wave across the globe. The Avengers joined forces with the X-Men to take the Red Onslaught down, but the two teams failed.[724] However, after Magneto assembled a team of supervillains to stop the Red Onslaught, the Scarlet Witch and Doctor Doom were able to cast an inversion spell to strengthen Charles Xavier's consciousness in his soul. As a collateral result, the moral axis of those present on the island was inverted, including the Avengers.[725]

Under the leadership of the new Captain America, an evil group of inverted Avengers decided to execute the Red Skull for his crimes.[726] To ensure their authority, they tricked most of the heroes of the world to attend a meeting at the Avengers Tower, where they were reduced in size and arrested by the inverted Avengers. Spider-Man and Nova managed to escape, joining Steve Rogers, Magneto and the inverted super villains. Meanwhile, the Scarlet Witch severed her alliance with the inverted Avengers, seeking revenge against Doctor Doom for their previous conflicts.[726] Doctor Doom, with S.H.I.E.L.D.'s assistance, gathered a group of Avengers to stop her.[727]

The Avengers found in the X-Men a violent opposition.[728] The villainous X-Men planned on detonating a gene bomb to kill everyone on the Earth who did not carry a mutant gene. Steve Rogers, Spider-Man and Magneto's team of villains tried to stop the X-Men.[729] Though defeated in combat,[730] they managed to prevent the bomb from fulfilling its purpose with Carnage's apparent sacrifice.[731] With humanity safe, the inverted Avengers battled the X-Men. During the fight, a reinversion spell was cast by the Scarlet Witch and Doctor Doom, with the help of the inverted Red Skull, which restored almost everybody back to normal. However, Iron Man, Sabretooth and Havok maintained their inverted personas as a result of a mechanism designed by the immoral Stark,[732] as a result Iron Man had his reason permanently deviated.[733] Around this period, the Hulk was treated with the Extremis virus and developed a new personality, which retained both physical strength and intelligence as Doc Green.[734]

Time Runs Out[]

With the Illuminati giving up on the possibility of destroying worlds to prevent incursions, ex-Illuminatus Namor assembled a Cabal of murderers who employed Antimatter Injection Systems to carry out the obliteration any and every alternate planet Earth that came in collision course with their own, keeping Earth spinning. Steve Rogers had the Avengers operate fully under S.H.I.E.L.D. to hunt down the Illuminati, an initiative that led the Avengers Machine to ruin. The charismatic Sunspot was one of the many members who left the group, ultimately purchasing A.I.M. to use their resources to tackle the incursions once the existence of this phenomena became public knowledge.[735] Part of Sunspot's own team of new Avengers explored the multiverse to assess the early death of existence. On Earth, A.I.M.'s Avengers used Ex Nihilo's systems to empower themselves to intervene in the war between S.H.I.E.L.D.'s Avengers and the Illuminati.[736]

The Avengers, working under S.H.I.E.L.D., guided by the Invisible Woman and counting with an army of War Machine drones, managed to capture the Illuminatus Amadeus Cho.[737] Able to pinpoint the Illuminati, S.H.I.E.L.D. led the Avengers to a battle against the Illuminati. The ensuing battle was revealed to be a trap.[738] As Sunspot and his Avengers attempted to prevent the teams from fighting each other, Steve Rogers called Cage's Avengers to join the fight. The Avengers' civil war was ultimately stopped by Invisible Woman, who revealed herself to have been in coalition with the Illuminati all along and forced a truce.[739]

Counting with a defective Namor, the heroes agreed that they should focus on putting the Cabal down. Setting a trap for the brutal team, Namor abandoned them in a terminal world during an incursion. However, Black Panther attacked Namor in order to execute him for his previous attacks against Wakanda.[740] With the Cabal dead, Avengers and Illuminati worked together to stop the collapse of the Multiverse. In his investigation, Illuminatus Hank Pym learned that the incursions were caused by the Beyonders, as part of one of their nefarious experiments.[741] Simultaneously, Doctor Strange learned that Doctor Doom had also been part of the incursions experiment, fighting a secret war against the Beyonders to sabotage their nefarious experiment.[742] The group of Avengers exploring the Multiverse tackled the Beyonders, being totally obliterated.[743] Following their demise, Doctor Doom, Doctor Strange and the Molecule Man directly confronted the Beyonders,[744] with Doom being able to seize their omnipotence for himself.[745]

Meanwhile, the Shi'ar Empire targeted Earth as the source of the incursions in order to eliminate the threat, gathering the Intergalactic Council and their armada in their attack. The Guardians of the Galaxy alerted the Avengers about the imminent attack.[746] The Illuminati broke Iron Man free from captivity set by the Cabal to combat the alien attack. Causing Earth to be replaced by the rogue planet, Iron Man got enough time to use his Sol's Hammer armor to win the battle. Back to Earth, Steve Rogers and Tony Stark solved their differences in a brutal fight as the last incursion between the two remaining universes was triggered.[747]

Since the end of existence was a matter of time, Reed Richards the Future Foundation chose not to lose instead of winning. Creating "life rafts" resistant to the incursion, the heroes attempted to ensure the survival of a few.[746] Both worlds were unable to prevent the collision and their universes were destroyed. Manifold assembled a team of heroes to a raft[745] emerging in a world created and ruled by Emperor Doom.[748] The Multiverse was ultimately returned to existence by Reed Richards using the power of the Molecule Man, following a conflict against Doctor Doom.[749] In the rebuilt reality, consequences and memories concerning the incursions were nebulous.[750]

A lot would change for the Avengers in the following eight months. As Thor was unworthy of his own divinity, a new Thor stepped in his place as the wielder of Mjolnir and Goddess of Thunder,[751] establishing herself as prominent warrior in the super hero community.[752] The new Thor joined the Avengers and so did the morally inverted and heroic Sabretooth, who was held caged and unleashed upon need by the Avengers. The team fought the artificial Descendants on A.I.M. Island, and Hank Pym inadvertently deactivated the opponents with a neural inhibitor, claiming that artificial life could not be murdered. This brought conflict with the Vision, an artificial man himself. Matters escalated when Ultron infected I.S.A.A.C. and Titan, prompting Starfox to search for the Avengers' help. Ultron moved his army of robotic drones to the Avengers Tower, infecting many Avengers with a virus. Pym and a group of Avengers managed to escape to Titan, retreating to the Church of Thanos to counter Ultron's plan of turning all life into robotic. The Vision wished to merge with Ultron to cleanse those afflicted from the infection. However, Hank Pym merged with his enraged creation instead. Infused by Starfox with feelings of love, the merged Ultron interrupted the infections and fled to space. Hank Pym was declared gone to the Avengers.[753]

Following all of their trials and tribulations, the Avengers as they formerly existed before ultimately were no more.[754] Black Panther formed an openly group to combat multiversal level threats as a replacement to the dark Illuminati, the Ultimates.[755] Meanwhile, Captain Marvel was in charge of the Alpha Flight Space Program to protect Earth from alien interventions;[756] the program was close to A-Force, an all-female super hero team assembled by the cosmic Singularity.[757] Sunspot officialized his Avengers team as A.I.M.'s Mightiest Heroes[758] and the Unity Division was rebranded as a team funded by the now popular Deadpool and directly approached the danger that the Terrigen Mists posed to mutants.[759]

All-New, All-Different[]

The Avengers eventually reunited by fate. A group of heroes joined forces to combat the threat of the Chitauri champion Warbringer, who wished to annihilate the human race in retaliation for having been beaten by Nova in the past, being assisted in his attack by the mysterious entrepreneur Mr. Gryphon, the new owner of the Avengers Tower. Iron Man and the new Captain America, right after deciding to reform the Avengers, stumbled upon Warbringer when he battled the teenager Spider-Man, a survivor of world Earth had collided with in the last incursion.[760] Assisted by the Vision, the Avengers searched for the Warbringer, who was collecting Chitauri artifacts for his purpose. They found the villain fighting the Inhuman Ms. Marvel and teenage rocket Nova. As the Warbringer caused immense devastation, the Avengers were occasionally joined by their last member, the new Thor.[761] Together, adult and teenage heroes successfully forced Warbringer through a portal he had intended to use to lead a Chitauri army to ravage Earth even though Gryphon kept sabotaging the heroes secretly. In the end, the Avengers officially reformed.[762]

The All-New, All-Different Avengers experienced an unglamorous start, as Iron Man lacked funding for the team, as a result of his negligence towards his finances for being a space hero for months. The team operated in a precarious New Jersey airfield warehouse known as the Avengers Hangar.[763] In their first mission, the Avengers battled Radioactive Man, who caused chaos in the name of the rising "Qeng Dinasty".[764] In a similar conflict, the group defeated Cyclone.[763] In the meantime, the teenager members of the team were discredited by the erratic Vision, who pushed Ms. Marvel out of the team and blackmailed Nova for hiding his previous interactions with the Warbringer. Another villain acting in the name of the "Qeng Dinasty" was Equinox. During the fight against him, the Avengers were ultimately betrayed by the Vision, who was revealed to have been under the control of Mr. Gryphon, one of Kang the Conqueror's many iterations.[765] Deprived of Mjolnir, Thor was revealed to Captain America to be cancer patient Doctor Jane Foster and helped her reacquire her powers. Meanwhile, Iron Man restored the Vision's faculties and the teenage Avengers assembled to defeat Gryphon, who was ultimately knocked out and lost in the timestream.[766]

Maria Hill had S.H.I.E.L.D. establish a secret brainwashing prison center for super powered criminals in the town of Pleasant Hill, a derivation of Project: Kobik, which employed a sentient Cosmic Cube to alter reality.[767] The illusory environment's existence was made known to Captain America by Rick Jones and to Steve Rogers by Bucky. As a S.H.I.E.L.D. commander, Rogers visited the prison with Hill when it was rioted by Baron Zemo, one of its inmates who had managed to overcome the reconditioning.[768] Both the Unity Division and the Avengers investigated the site but were ultimately trapped in the illusion.[769]

Unity Division's leader Rogue managed to see through the fake setting and helped her teammates see through the lies.[770] The Avengers were caught in a violent battle against Zemo's army of prisoners. As Kobik had assumed the form of a little girl, she was unable to witness the Avengers suffering and returned them to their former and fully empowered selves.[771] She also restored Steve Rogers to full vigor,[772] allowing him to bring the battle to Baron Zemo. An enraged Kobik cast Zemo away, and the Avengers focused on stopping the super villains in the riot, who were defeated by S.H.I.E.L.D. agent, the new Quasar. In the end, Steve Rogers and Sam Wilson decided to share the mantle of Captain America in their respective Avengers teams.[773] Unexpectedly, as per the machinations of the Red Skull, Steve Rogers was reconfigured as a Hydra agent, infiltrated in S.H.I.E.L.D. and in the Avengers with the mission of bringing up a Hydra empire to replace the United States.[774]

Rogue intercepted an amicable Hank Pym by chance, assembling the Unity Division to assess the situation.[775] They ultimately came to the conclusion that Ultron was in control of their merged body.[776] The Vision assembled all available Avengers to war Ultron one more time.[777] Iron Man trapped Ultron inside a Hulkbuster Armor in order to bring the battle to outer space. Following a difficult fight, the Avengers sent Ultron to his ultimate fate in the sun.[778] Soon after, the group was approached by a young girl named Nadia, who claimed to be Pym's daughter and a Red Room Academy fugitive. As the new and unstoppable Wasp, she proved her worth in helping the Vision overcome problems related to Kang's tampering.[779]

As Jarvis introduced Nadia to the original Wasp, the Avengers decided to look for Nova's missing father in outer space. In their mission, they found a miserable planet struggling with abductions to the Negative Zone performed by Annihilus, as he attempted to build an apparatus to unleash his wrath upon the multiverse.[780] The Avengers assembled and, wielding Captain Mar-Vell's former Nega Bands that had been seized by Annihilus, foiled his plans and severed his connection to the universe.[781]

Hydra Empire[]

The Avengers experienced fractures in their alliances due to ideological stances. With the manifestation of an Inhuman clairvoyant named Ulysses, Captain Marvel operated Alpha Flight, A-Force and the Ultimates to act preventively, in order to avoid crimes, a position Iron Man radically opposed to.[782] Predicting Thanos would invade Project Pegasus for a Cosmic Cube, Captain Marvel led a squad to attack him. In the fight, War Machine was murdered, and She-Hulk was critically injured.[783] Iron Man kidnapped Ulysses to study him, prompting the Inhumans and Captain Marvel to hunt him. The heroes then learned the Hulk was an imminent and deadly threat to them.[784] Hawkeye put the Hulk down,[785] but was judged innocent. The Hulk's death escalated tensions into a second superhuman civil war as Iron Man actively attempted to stop Captain Marvel, having the Avengers at his side.[786]

In a subsequent vision, the heroes learned that the Avenger Spider-Man would be responsible for the death of Steve Rogers in Washington, D.C..[787] Iron Man and the Avengers vehemently opposed to Captain Marvel's intentions of putting him under preventive arrest and escaped. However, the young heroes associated with the Avengers questioned their recent actions and disbanded.[788] In Washington, D.C., Spider-Man and Steve Rogers met to solve the situation, leading to both Iron Man and Captain Marvel to intervene.[789] Captain Marvel brutally stroke at Iron Man, essentially causing him to fall into a death-like state.[790] In the aftermath of the war, Hawkeye wandered the country to bring vengeance to the people,[791] a bunch of former Avengers banded together as the Defenders operating in the urban setting of Manhattan,[792] the disillusioned younger Avengers Ms. Marvel, Spider-Man and Nova formed their own super hero group, the Champions,[793] and, more dangerously, Steve Rogers made his way to gain absolute power and ensure Hydra's gradual ascension.[794]

The Avengers maintained their operations, recruiting Hercules to replace the heroes who had left to the Champions. Being offered funding by Parker Industries, they relocated to the Baxter Building and had the original Spider-Man back to the team, as he acted as Parker Industries' private hero. The group was attacked by Kang and the Scarlet Centurion,[795] in retaliation for the Vision kidnapping their newborn self after Mr. Gryphon's manipulations.[796] The time travelers paid back in the same coin and erased the Avengers from existing by capturing their baby selves.[795] The Avengers were preserved by a future version of Kang, while Hercules as the last Avenger remaining confronted the villains in the Temple of Pama for the baby.[797] The Wasp traveled to the future with the baby Kang to prevent the paradoxical collapse of the timestream, being assisted by the future Priests of Pama in fully restoring the Avengers. After returning the baby to his proper place, the Avengers decided to vanquish Kang for good.[798] Recruiting different groups from different points from the past, the Avengers assembled an intertemporal mighty team to attack Kang in different eras.[799] In the end, the original Giant-Man used Kang's future stealing machine against himself, and the Avengers, but the Vision, returned home with no recollection of their paradoxal war against Kang.[800]

Due to a number of unexplainable magical disturbances, Doctor Doom contacted the Avengers for help. The Avengers found child sorceresses who worship Anamelech as the responsible for the incidents and put an end to their actions.[801] Back home, the Avengers were attacked by Cressida, the Avenger X, an old enemy of theirs with power stealing abilities who had been entombed by the Wizard and was reawakened by Kang's tampering with the timestream. With the Avengers defeated, the Wasp called Doom for help, and they managed to trap Cressida in the Microverse.[802]

S.H.I.E.L.D. commander Steve Rogers soon executed his plan to take over the United States for Hydra. He summoned a Chitauri invasion and shielded Earth against, leaving Captain Marvel, Alpha Flight, the Ultimates, the Guardians of the Galaxy and many cosmic heroes trapped on Earth's orbit to fight against endless hordes. Simultaneously, Pleasant Hill's criminals ravaged New York City. When local heroes such as Doctor Strange, the Defenders, the X-Men and the Unity Division intervened, they were trapped inside a Darkforce impenetrable dome cast by a Darkhold empowered Blackout.[803] As Supreme Hydra, Rogers ruled the country with absolute control with his High Council. The Avengers and the Champions were easily defeated, with Thor being banished, the Vision being corrupted by Arnim Zola, and the Scarlet witch being possessed by Chthon.[804] Supreme Hydra assembled his own team of Hydra Avengers and brutally killed Rick Jones, while Hawkeye and Black Widow retreated to lead the Underground resistance movement, supported by a Tony Stark A.I..[805]

As Hydra destroyed Las Vegas to attract the Underground, a schism took place: Black Widow chose to assassinate Rogers and recruited the Champions to her new Red Room, while Hawkeye and the Avengers wished to revert the effects of the Kobik Cosmic Cube, which had been fragmented, and approached Sam Wilson, the former Captain America, to help them.[806] In the Alaskan Ultronic Territories, Hydra Avengers and the Underground Avengers looked for a Cosmic Cube fragment. An insane Ultron, who had managed to return to Earth, did not allow the two groups to fight each other. After a confrontation over Hank Pym's past mistakes, the fragment was given to Underground member Ant-Man. After the Avengers groups returned to their quest, Namor provided Hydra with another fragment.[807]

The Underground kept failing at finding more fragments and returned to their base, where Hydra unleashed the rage of a momentarily resurrected Hulk upon them. The group was fragilized due to secrets and blackmailing and took a deep hit. The Underground managed to escape, but their base was utterly destroyed, and Supreme Hydra acquired the fragments of the Cosmic Cube.[808] Black Widow and Spider-Man went to the Capitol, where Steve Rogers was supposed to be assassinated as per Ulysses' former vision. However, Black Widow was killed instead, prompting a direct war between Hydra and the Underground and Sam Wilson to reclaim the Captain America mantle.[809] Inspired by Captain America, the heroes overcame Hydra's attack. Quasar obliterated the shield that enveloped Earth and Maria Hill executed Blackout, liberating New York City and its heroes trapped in the dark.[810] The Avengers reassembled in Washington, D.C. and launched a direct offensive on Hydra's regime. Unexpectedly, Supreme Hydra was empowered by the Cosmic Cube,[811] and reshaped reality to fit his Hydra ideals. Being tricked by Captain America, Supreme Hydra witnessed the return of Kobik and the original version of Steve Rogers. Hydra was then deposed, ending the group's control over the United States and Earth's Mightiest Heroes standing triumphant.[812]

No Surrender, No Road Home[]

Hydra's rule brought the collapse of Parker Industries at the hands of Doctor Octopus. Losing funding and the Baxter Building, the Avengers resisted and relocated to G.I.R.L. Labs. Captain America returned to his Falcon identity, still as the leader of the group.[813] Both the Avengers and the Champions noticed spatial disturbances related to the existence of the High Evolutionary's planet, the Counter-Earth. In an uneasy team-up, the groups assessed the situation.[814] Falcon and the Vision's daughter, the Champion Viv, were transported to Counter-Earth as a result of its phasing effect on Earth[815] and experimented by the Evolutionary.[816] Fighting the Evolutinary's New Men, the Avengers and the Champions battled to prevent the collision and merger of Earth and Counter-Earth and rescued their teammates.[817] With Viv's apparent sacrifice the collision was prevented.[818] The Avengers and the Champions celebrated her return following an adventure that eased their previous animosity.[819]

A calamity took place when Earth was translocated from its position, prompting all branches of the Avengers to convene to respond to multiple disasters. Jarvis was gravely wounded in one of the crises. Additionally, most of Earth's super heroes were trapped in a static state except for some few Avengers, who were assembled by the original Avenger Voyager in the Avengers Mansion.[820] Voyager had been missing and forgotten for years, returning to tend to Earth being sequestered to serve as the battleground for a contest that had the new Lethal Legion and the Black Order as respective players[821] for the Elders Grandmaster and Challenger. With the Mansion destroyed by their adversaries, the Avengers retreated to the Avengers Auxiliary Headquarters.[822] By fighting the villains, they learned about the game of collecting the cosmic Pyramoids to score points.[823]

Scoring points at the cost of the Human Torch and the Red Wolf being out of the game, the Avengers entered the quest for the Pyramoids.[824] To combat them, the Challenger revived the Hulk. Meanwhile, with the Beast and the Wasp restoring Jarvis to consciousness, he alerted them that Voyager was a trickster. In fact, she was Grandmaster's daughter and his secret gamble in the contest and managed to acquire the last and deciding Pyramoid.[825] As the Hulk brutally slaughtered the Avengers and destroyed the Pyramoid, Voyager unexpectedly betrayed her father and sided with Earth's Mightiest Heroes.[826]

Since the Elders saw Earth as a mere disposable gaming board, the Avengers had to win the contest. Challenger brought his might to the planet and the Hulk counterattacked him, enraged for having been manipulated. Meanwhile, Quicksilver deactivated the beacon that kept the heroes in stasis, allowing Voyager to assemble an army of Avengers to the fight the Challenger.[827] As the Avengers defeated him, the hero Lightning placed his bets against the Grandmaster for Earth's fate, guaranteeing its return to its proper place.[828] Following the end of the game and the Avengers' victory, the different Avengers teams disbanded for different reasons.[829]

For the period Earth was away from the Solar System, the Goddess of the Night Nyx was able to boost her power and get revenge against the Olympian Gods who had imprisoned her and her children. As she cast an eternal night over the universe, Voyager assembled a group of Avengers to combat her.[830] Her power had been shattered to three pieces and scattered across different locations and the Avengers attempted to outran her in obtaining her full power.[831] Their quest led them to the Hyborian Age, where they joined Conan the Barbarian to fight the Goddess of the Night.[832] On Earth, Blue Marvel and Toni Ho dealt with the darkness with their Avengers World project. On Euphoria, Nyx gained full power and accessed the House of Ideas, the core of creation, in an attempt to obliterate all of the existence.[833] In the end, the Vision heroically assembled a legion of marvelous heroes at a conceptual level. Nyx perished and her darkness was cast out.[834] Conan stayed in the present and gradually teamed up with a bunch of individuals who eventually became a savage assembly of Avengers.[835]

Earth's Mightiest Legacy[]

Since Loki managed to release the fallen Celestial Zgreb from its ancient tomb, All-Father Odin cautiously advised the Black Panther about how the vile god had been defeated by Earth's first heroes, the prehistoric Avengers.[836] The reawakening of the first super villain coincided with Steve Rogers' glorious return as Captain America,[837] Tony Stark's full recovery as the Invincible Iron Man,[838] and Thor's reclaim of his name.[839] As the three classic Avengers discussed reassembling the group, Loki's activities sparked the arrival of the world-threatening Dark Celestials, the Final Host. Captain Marvel identified the threat and joined the Avengers in protecting Earth from falling Celestial corpses. At the same time, Black Panther recruited Doctor Strange to assess the tomb of the fallen Celestial. The cause of Celestials being infected, the parasitic Horde, attacked them alongside the new Ghost Rider and Jennifer Walters, who, as the Hulk, was imbued with an additional dose of gamma radiation by the moribund Celestial Eson to join the fight.[840]

In the North Pole, Captain America was introduced by Loki to the corpse of the long-time dead Progenitor, the Celestial who sparked the emergence of super humans on Earth. Meanwhile, the other Avengers assembled to search for ways to stop the Dark Celestial invasion. Iron Man and Doctor Strange were granted knowledge by the Eternals, Thor and Hulk were boosted by the Blood of Ymir, Black Panther and Captain Marvel were able to counter the Horde, and the Ghost Rider rescued Captain America.[841] By forming an Eternal-like Uni-Mind, the Avengers assembled their mighty powers and obliterated the Horde and the Dark Celestials. As such, the machinations of a defeated Loki assembled the Avengers one more time to carry on the legacy of the first super humans on the planet.[842] The grateful Celestials took custody of Loki and set upright the corpse of the Progenitor, which was refurbished and transformed by Wakandan architects, Alpha Flight technicians and Tony Stark into the Avengers Mountain, Earth's Mightiest Heroes' global headquarters. Black Panther was unanimously appointed as the chairperson to the revamped team[843] and created the secret Agents of Wakanda as a covert operation to complement the Avengers in an attempt to upgrade their network to international level. Ken Hale, the Gorilla-Man, was in charge of taking care of the Mountain.[844]

There were unfriendly forces to the Avengers in the world, though. Responding to their first crisis, the Avengers confronted Namor, who declared war on humanity alongside his Defenders of the Deep following Roxxon's reckless contamination of the aquatic fragilized environment.[845] During a fight in a stormed Hydropolis, the Avengers' fight against the Defenders escalated with the presence of the Winter Guard led by the Red Widow, who also tackled Namor for his war crimes. With Namor's retreat, the Avengers ceased fire. Meanwhile, the Avengers being led by the King of Wakanda displeased Washington, D.C.; thus, as a response to the rise of super human teams around the world, Phil Coulson formed America's Mightiest Heroes, the Squadron Supreme,[846] under Mephisto's tutelage.[847]

Witnessing the escalation of a chaotic vampire civil war, Black Panther had his agents rescue and recruit vampire slayer Blade to the Avengers.[844] As the lord of the vampires Dracula sought the Winder Guard's help and was contacted by Iron Man, the other side of the conflict, in the form of Shadow Colonel and his Legion of the Unliving, were approached by the Avengers, infiltrating the Avengers Mountain and corrupting the Ghost Rider to their cause.[848] After Blade managed to purge the corruption from Ghost Rider,[849] he led the Avengers to stop the Shadow Colonel, ultimately seizing his Boy-Thing. In the end, the hellhound Sarge was defeated by Thor's pet hound Thori and kept captive in the Avengers Mountain and Dracula secretly won the war, establishing a vampire nation in Chernobyl due to Winter Guard's inefficiency in keeping him.[850]

War of the Realms[]

Laying waste to the Ten Realms, Malekith the Accursed and his Dark Council brought a war to Midgard, the realm of mortal Earth. As his first move, Malekith trapped Thor in the land of the Frost Giants, Jotunheim. Without Thor, the Avengers tackled the invasion in New York City.[851] Doctor Strange evacuated all heroes and victims to the Avengers Mountain, and Malekith's forces conquered the world.[852] As Black Panther and Iron Man protected the Avengers Mountain, the other Avengers splintered their might into successful Strikeforces. One led by Captain America to rescue Thor in Jotunheim, another led by Lady Freyja to sabotage the villains' Black Bifrost transport in Svartalfheim and the War Avengers led by Captain Marvel to resist the invasion on Earth.[853]

The Avengers were reassembled by Freyja at the Avengers Mountain alongside an army of champions from many realms to combat the siege. Inspired by Jane Foster and led by Thor,[854] who respectively wielded the All-Weapon Undrjarn and the worthy Mjolnir, the Avengers took part in ending the war of the Ten Realms. As a result, Thor was coronated All-Father,[855] Jane Foster lived up to the legacy of the Valkyrie name.[856] and Blade was involved in assembling band of randomly implicated heroes who operated as Strikeforce.[857]

When the Ghost Rider's Hell Charger acted erratically, the Avengers summoned demonologist Daimon Hellstrom for help. During the exorcism, the first modern Ghost Rider and King of Hell, Johnny Blaze, challenged the Avenger Ghost Rider for a race over power.[858] King Blaze wished to obtain power to combat Mephisto. The Avengers Mountain was possessed,[859] and the invading entity was revealed by Boy-Thing to be the Cosmic Ghost Rider, who had been manipulated by Blaze to achieve his objectives, but decided to help the Avengers instead.[860] In Hell, the Avengers rescued their teammate Ghost Rider after he had beaten King Blaze in the race.[861]

With the first rumors of a new Starbrand since the death of Kevin Connor, the Avengers embarked on a mission to look for Earth's new protector, finding themselves in the Shi'ar Ravenstarr Maximum-Security Prison Galaxy being hunted by the Heralds of Galactus, who were also looking for the Starbrand power.[862] With the Black Widow wearing a War Machine Armor and Blade wearing Boy-Thing and his burning touch, the Avengers resisted the Heralds.[863] The power was found by Shi'ar Majestor Gladiator within a pregnant human inmate who perished after Captain America delivered her baby, the new Starbrand, and brought her to the Avengers Mountain.[864]

Empyre[]

A distress call led the Avengers to the Blue Area of the Moon, which had been reforested as a garden by the actions of the elder Cotati Swordsman and his child with the Celestial Madonna Mantis, Quoi the Celestial Messiah. Having fended off an attack by a Kree Sentry, Earth's Mightiest Heroes decided to help the Cotati against the Kree/Skrull Alliance,[865] a cojoined empire ruled by Captain Mar-Vell's hybrid son and former Young Avenger Emperor Hulkling.[866] The Alliance's massive fleet was targeted by the Avengers as Iron Man overloaded their systems, allowing the Cotati to bloom the Death Blossom and massacre them. Revealing their plan to avenge the slaughter of their ancestors and conquer the entire universe, the Celestial Messiah announced that Earth, the Avengers World, was the first to succumb to their rising empyrean, much to the dismay of the Avengers.[867] Thor, Iron Man, and Captain America were captured, but refused to surrender and managed to escape to Earth, where the Black Panther, the Hulk and the Ghost Rider dealt with the Cotati's overrunning invasion. Meanwhile, Captain Marvel approached the Alliance, who had been assisted by the Fantastic Four to cleanse the Cotati infection. She was made an Accuser by Hulkling to combat the Cotati.[868] Captain America and Black Panther ordered the Avengers and the Agents of Wakanda to fend off the endless armies of Cotati around the world.[869]

While Iron Man and Reed Richards formulated a plan to defeat the Cotati, Black Panther organized the Wakandan troops to prevent the aliens from using the Vibranium enriched soil of the Great Mound.[870] Unpredictably, Emperor Hulkling decided to fire the Pyre, a solar doomsday weapon that would raze Earth to end the Cotati. Captain Marvel and Human Torch approached Wiccan, as Hulkling's husband, for help. Meanwhile, Mantis contacted her son to stop the invasion, but the Avengers were betrayed by the Hulk, who had been murdered and replaced by a Cotati.[871] Wiccan exposed that Emperor Hulkling had been impersonated by his Skrull grandmother, R'Klll, but the Pyre had already been activated in the Sun. With Black Panther defeated, the Celestial Messiah planted a Death Blossom on Vibranium to boost his empyrean invasion.[872] Wiccan, Captain Marvel, Human Torch and the Alliance attempted to tame the Sun, being successful due to the contribution of Iron Man. The Invisible Woman, the Thing and Mantis defeated the infected Hulk, followed by Black Panther, Reed Richards and Captain America assembling the Avengers to finish the Cotati and their Messiah. Being empowered by the magic of his birth Mother Gaea, Thor cleansed the planet of the vegetative infection. The Black Panther then destroyed the Death Blossom and the plant empire was left in ruins.[873]

In Mephisto we distrust[]

In between the Avengers' cosmic adventures, it was revealed that Mephisto had been manipulating Earth's Mightiest Heroes since the Stone Age. He trapped and tempted Iron Man for months in the distant past,[861] and influenced the Avengers' adversaries in the present.[874] Wishing to stop Mephisto, the lunatic vigilante Moon Knight set up a plan to seize the primordial powers of the prehistoric Avengers. His victims were Iron Fist, Doctor Strange as the Sorcerer Supreme, Ghost Rider as the Spirit of Vengeance, Black Panther and Thor as the God of Thunder.[875] Earth's Mightiest Hero Moon Knight apparently murdered Mephisto in his captivity in Hotel Inferno, reshaped New York City as the glory of the Moon god Khonshu and tortured the Black Panther to claim his power. The Avengers resisted[876] and rescued the powerless and trapped heroes as Khonshu endlessly slayed Mephistos of the interdimensional Council of Red with the primordial powers.[877] Black Panther ultimately defeated Moon Knight, who killed himself[878] to ascend as the host of the Phoenix and rebel against his idol Khonshu. The Avengers were able return the stolen powers and arrest Khonshu, while Thor knocked out Moon Knight,[879] who later refused Black Panther's offer to join the Avengers.[880]

The Phoenix then built a nest on Earth,[880] ultimately sparking a tournament and collecting champions to choose its next host. The battle for the Phoenix counted with many empowered contestants. The Black Panther was chosen a favorite candidate by the fiery bird, although he feared succumbing to it.[881] Meanwhile, urban martial artist Echo was murdered in a round against Namor.[882] The Avengers left out of the tournament unsuccessfully attempted to tame the Phoenix.[883] In the end of the contest, Echo was reborn and recollected the Phoenix's shards to become its host.[884]

Around this period, Earth's Mightiest Heroes also combated the invasion of hordes of Symbiotes orchestrated by the king in black Knull. They sent the Sentry to tackle the villain, but he was easily killed off. Earth fell as a world in the dark.[885] Many heroes were infected by Symbiotes as Iron Man devised a plan to hack the invaders[886] and Thor brought the fight directly to Knull.[887] The heroes broke free from Kull's control through the efforts of Dylan Brock, the son of Venom, who in turn ascended as the new Captain Universe with the help of the Silver Surfer and Reed Richards.[888] Knull and his hordes were obliterated and Earth cleansed of his infection. For the war, Blade had recruited vampires from Dracula's nation in Chernobyl, but turned against them as the conflict was over.[889] This caused an international incident to the Avengers as Dracula's Vampire Nation had gained recognition as a country. The Avengers diplomatically had Blade act as a sheriff in the Vampire Nation as a response.[890]

Using Mephisto's cubic Hellahedron to change the world, Phil Coulson reshaped existence, transforming himself into the President of the United States and having the Supreme Squadron of America as the mightiest super hero group of the world. Immune to the alterations,[891] Blade woke up in the twisted world with no vestige of the Avengers or Wakanda. After meeting up with that reality version of Nighthawk, Blade averred that the world was a travesty and decided to assemble the Avengers, starting by releasing Captain America from the icecap he had never been freed from.[892] With Captain America convinced,[893] their first recruit was the Phoenix Echo, who had been kept in the Ravencroft Institute.[894] Simultaneously, the Black Panther recruited the child Starbrand,[895] being eventually approached by Blade's team.[896] As a final member, they had Thor. Their assembly caught the attention of the Squadron Supreme,[897] prompting a fight between the two groups.[898] Captain America directly fought Coulson, who attempted to use the hellish cube to sustain the skewed reality. Defeated, Coulson was abandoned by Mephisto, and reality was restored to its proper self with the destruction of the Hellahedron. In the restored world, Starbrand kept her form as a child and Nighthawk questioned the motivations of his superiors.[891]

Betrayed by Ken Hale, the Avengers were attacked in their Mountain by the Winter Guard, who kidnapped the Hulk.[899] They went to her rescue weeks later, in a confrontation that permanently incapacitated the Winter Guard. However, the mental conditioning turned Jen Walters into the Winter Hulk.[900] Forcing Ken Hale to assist her, the Winter Hulk ravaged the Vampire Nation and moved her rage to Atlantis,[901] where she assembled the Avengers and was revealed to have been a sleeper agent all along as part of a secret mission envisioned by herself and the Black Panther.[902] The Hulk siphoned the energy of the gamma bomb that the Winter Guard planned to use to destroy Atlantis. With Atlantis safe, the Hulk liberated the excessive radiation in the Avengers Mountain and returned to her sensational usual self as She-Hulk, requesting a leave of absence from the team. She suggested the grateful Namor to redeem himself by joining the Avengers.[903]

In order to castrate the legacy of heroes being assembled across the times, Mephisto influenced a time-traveling Doom Supreme to do the same by assembling the almighty multiversal Masters of Evil to eliminate the very concept of super heroes in several realities and ultimately ascend as the malignant lords of many Earths. To combat the Masters of Evil, the "Avenger Prime" had Deathloks as his intertemporal agents, who contacted Namor and the Valkyrie Jane Foster to join the Avengers. Upon their first contact in the Avengers Mountain, the Ghost Rider was transported by one Deathlok to assemble Avengers across the Multiverse as the All-Rider. Meanwhile, Doom's Masters sought to eliminate these Deathloks.[903] The Masters brutally attacked the Avengers in different locations to destroy the Deathloks,[904] ultimately choosing to retreat after killing all of their targets and detonating the Avengers Mountain.[905]

Following Black Panther's resignation as chairman and a conflict against the worshippers of Mephisto, the Serpent Society, the Avengers welcomed Nighthawk to their ranks to combat the Red Council.[906] Using the Progenitor's technology, the Avengers embarked in a journey across time to protect the legacy of super-heroics from Mephisto and the Masters of Evil.[907] During World War II, they helped the Secret Invaders resist Mephisto's influence.[908] In feudal Japan, they learned from the Ghost Ronin that they needed to reach the Avengers from pre-history.[909] In the Old West, when teaming up with Reno Phoenix and the Starbrand Kid, the Avengers found a Mephisto again.
