This time, Starbrand was able to tackle the devil.[910] At the cost of her own life force, Starbrand eradicated Mephistos from different moments of history. Due to her efforts, the Avengers arrived at the correct destination.[907] Finally, the Avengers met their counterparts from 1,000,000 years ago.[911] Unfortunately, in their arrogance, the two groups of Avengers clashed with each other, leaving them vulnerable to Doom Supreme and the Masters of Evil.[912] However, by sharing a common enemy, they assembled as one group of Avengers to fight their vile enemies. Although some Masters of Evil were destroyed, so were some of the prehistoric Avengers.[913] The Masters of Evil were defeated, but Doom Supreme, counting with a legion of alternate Dooms, prepared himself for retaliation.[914]

Simultaneously, Avenger Prime directly confronted the Red Council. His army of Avengers from different universes gathered by the All-Rider fought the Mephistos in the Avengers Tower located in the God Quarry.[912] Doom Supreme and his alternate allies intervened, prompting Avenger Prime to join the fight and reveal his true identity: Loki, the one who always leads the Avengers to assemble.[915] Avenger Prime Loki was able to stop the siege staged by Doom and transport the Avengers from present and pre-history to join his Multiversal Avengers[916] to fight the several variants of Doctor Doom.[917] Mephisto took the opportunity to usurp power from the Council of Red to ascend to power. To oppose him, a Deathlok uploaded himself into Avengers Mountain,[918] and the Celestial corpse was remodelled by Gorilla-Man into a Deathlok.[919] The battle caused the imminent collapse of the God Quarry and punctured a hole to the First Firmament, whose overflowing power threatened the entire Multiverse. The Avengers split their attention to combat their enemies and repair the entropic damage. Their multiversal assembly finished Doom Supreme and banished Mephisto, stabilized the God Quarry and saved the worlds ravaged by the Masters of Evil, though at the cost of the All-Rider and of the Starbrand. Having honored their lost comrades, the Avengers prepared themselves to rebrand their team.[920]

Tribulation Events[]

Captain Marvel was elected to become the new chairperson of the Avengers, who enjoyed the amenities of the Jarvis Lounge to gather up. Selecting an iconic group of former Avengers, Captain Marvel wished to preventively protect Earth. Their first battle was against Terminus, who ravaged Project: P.E.G.A.S.U.S. in search for an energy source. In the middle of the fight, Captain Marvel was transported through a disrupted black hole generator out of time and space only to meet Kang the Conqueror,[921] who had just been lethally wounded by the Twilight Court, a group of heroes crafted by the mysterious Myrddin to access the so-called tribulation events and acquire the Missing Moment. Since Kang also wanted the Missing Moment as prize, he had plans of using an analogous superhero team, just like the Avengers, for his purposes.[922] With Kang's privileged intel about the future, Captain Marvel was able to coordinate the Avengers in several lifesaving operations.[923]

As their first tribulation event, the Avengers faced the Ashen Combine, a group of city-killers who split up around the globe to ravage the planet. While most Avengers resisted their attacks individually, Captain America and the Black Panther gathered intel by infiltrating their opponents' base on Earth's Orbit, the Impossible City, a sentient infrastructure who had been enslaved by the villains.[924] By outsmarting and arresting each of the Ashen Combine's members, the Avengers emerged victorious and liberated the Impossible City, who became their new headquarters.[925]

The Avengers fell to an oneiric trap cast by Nightmare in the Impossible City. The Vision and the Scarlet Witch were able to evade it, only to learn the attack had been schemed by Myrddin and his Twilight Court.[926] While the duo struggled against the Twilight Court, who wished to end Kang, Nightmare bargained for the freedom of the rest of the team,[927] ultimately insinuating all of existence would be in peril in the near future.[928] With the scales evened up, the Avengers bested their rivals by attacking the exact opponents who were not prepared for their capacities.[929] However, Myrddin was able to strip Kang from the privileged knowledge he had about the tribulation events. As a consequence, an upset Kang decided to sever his alliance with Avengers, once again declaring them as mortal enemies.[928] With the rise of the anti-mutant organization Orchis, the Avengers set up as their priority liberating incarcerated mutants and keeping them safe in the Impossible City. One of Orchis' leaderships, M.O.D.O.K., retaliated, being backed up by former and traitorous Avenger Triathlon, now the 3D-Man. By sending deadly Stark Sentinels to the Impossible City, M.O.D.O.K. caused major problems. In fact, 3D-Man was a deep undercover and hypnotized mole inside Orchis, who returned to his senses after the Black Panther intervened.[930]

One World Under Doom[]

Earth was engulfed in darkforce, allowing a legion of vampires to bring mayhem at a global level. After being contacted by Blade, the Avengers were ambushed by the Bloodcoven, who brutally maimed Thor and the Black Panther. Blade was revealed to be the leader of the massive invasion, slaying Doctor Strange as a precaution.[931] Cast out of the Impossible City and witnessing the Black Panther become a vampire loyal to Blade, the Avengers regrouped in Strange's Sanctum Sanctorum.[932] It was revealed Blade had been possessed by the first vampire, Varnae, who planned to bring absolute darkness upon the universe. The Black Panther overcame the infection, while Thor broke himself free, reassembling the Avengers to oppose the undead mastermind.[933] Varnae was defeated by the efforts of the Avengers, but his actions were only reversed thanks to Doctor Strange relinquishing his position as Sorcerer Supreme to Doctor Doom. The world was saved, but it owed a debt to Doom.[934]

During the crisis sparked by the vampire invasion, the Avengers Priority Call was activated, leading Steve Rogers to assemble a group of Avengers formed by Hercules, the new Hawkeye, Quicksilver, and Hazmat, to protect innocents on Earth, while Captain Marvel led the Avengers to the main battle. Realizing hostages were being collected by a faction, these Avengers were pulled onto a Helicarrier run by Baron Blood.[935] The Avengers freed the captive civilians and took control over the Helicarrier.[936] Baron Blood was defeated as his lackeys perished in the mission.[937] This mission led to the formation of the Avengers Emergency Response Squad, a.k.a. Aveng.E.R.S., an initiative formed by a constantly transitional team of Avengers based at the Avengers Mansion.[938] Following the vampiric crisis, which was a Tribulation Event, Captain America invited Storm back to the Avengers in search for mutant representation.[939] She accepted the offer and replaced Thor in the team. This coincided with the version of Hyperion from Mephisto's world targeting Earth. With assistance from the X-Men, Doctor Strange, and Asgard, the Avengers banished Hyperion to a universe destroyed by the Ashen Combine before he could act.[940] In Cyclops and his X-Men, after a long time of tense interactions, the Avengers finally found close allies and friends.[941]

Keeping track of Kang's actions, the Avengers prepared to collect a piece of arcane data that once belonged to him that was about to be auctioned in a casino belonging to Grandmaster. Performing an elaborate ruse, the Avengers learned Kang worked in coalition with the master thief Black Cat.[942] By hunting Kang, the Avengers faced the group of mercenaries he had hired, the bizarre Technet. Although the Avengers defeated the goons, Kang was able to use the device to summon an army of followers.[943] Kang's army ravaged the Grandmaster's Speculatorium as the Avengers became trapped within his warship. As the Black Cat betrayed her ally in favor of the Avengers, they reacquired the codex. Ultimately, the Grandmaster, with Myrddin's help, cast Kang out of his empire, allowing the Avengers to return home.[944]

As a great influence in the world, Doctor Doom assembled the Avengers to question them about their constant failures in improving the world as its allegedly sworn protectors. In this setting, Doctor Doom realized he should act where the Avengers would not.[945] He announced his intentions of seizing rule over the world, having as one of his first actions the extermination of Hydra, earning him immense credibility. The Avengers assembled many heroes of the world, including the Fantastic Four, to counter Doctor Doom's plans[946] by doing the unthinkable in teaming up with a legion of villainous elements.[947] In Castle Doom, Latveria, the Avengers learned in disbelief with their strike that all of Doctor Doom's actions were legit.[948] For a world under Doctor Doom's rule, Kristoff Vernard assembled a team of Superior Avengers with time-travelling individuals waring villainous mantles to act as Doom's Mightiest Heroes.[949]

The Mad Thinker, who had gained a recent interest in the Impossible City,[950] took Doom's ascension as an opportunity to reform the Masters of Evil and resist his influence. They managed to colonize the Impossible City and transform it into an independent nation out of Doctor Doom's jurisdiction. Being the only Avenger on site to recover from injuries when battling Doctor Doom, Captain America merged with the only remaining sliver of the Impossible City's consciousness to combat the Masters,[951] being joined in his mission by the Black Panther[952] and successfully defeating the Masters of Evil.[953] However, being empowered with Super-Adaptoid technology, the Mad Thinker resisted, until being surprised by the Impossible City restoring its functions and the Avengers returning to their base to finish him.[954]

As Earth's Sorcerer Supreme, Doctor Doom's duties led him to protect the planet from the dread Dormammu, who had banished the Avengers from their realm. Seeing how adamant Doctor Doom was to stop the threat, the Avengers, who had been freed from banishment, ultimately decided to support their nemesis after being broken free.[955] Dormammu was obliterated, leading the Avengers to question themselves about Doctor Doom's intentions and possibly positive impact in his position as the ruler of a unified world. However, Maria Hill emerged to prove Doctor Doom deployed immoral methods to accomplish his goals.[956] By infiltrating Latveria, the Avengers learned his omnipotence was harvested from the life force of his citizens. With the truth exposed, Doctor Doom unleashed his fury upon Earth's Mightiest Heroes. Public opinion about the morality of Doom's actions was divided as the Avengers were joined by the X-Men and the Fantastic Four in openly battling him.[957] In an immense display of power, Doctor Doom destroyed his enemies, but accidentally slew his goddaughter Val Richards in the process.[958] In desperation and regret, he abdicated his infinite powers and complete influence to resurrect her by sacrificing his own life.[959]

The Missing Moment[]

The Avengers consulted Reed Richards about Kang's objective concerning the Missing Moment, concluding it concerned the restoration of the Multiverse following the destruction of Doctor Doom's Battleworld. It represented a flaw created when Richards reformed existence.[960] Now knowing where to strike, the Avengers ventured through the cosmos until finding a cosmic rupture in the fabric of the universe. By joining their powers to pass through the rift, they arrived on Sub Rosa, the no-place of the universe, which contained the remnants of Battleworld. There, Myrddin surprise the Avengers, revealing he had already acquired the Missing Moment and the capacity of resetting the Multiverse in his twisted image. As Hyperion joined the Avengers in fighting Myrddin, the cunning villain revealed his real identity as a version of Kang, the Conqueror.[961] Being overpowered by Myrddin and his horde of undead superhumans, the Avengers were surprised by the Impossible City. In fact, it was Camelot, the Twilight Court's original headquarters.[962] Having learned of their creator's vile intentions, the Twilight Court had been banished to the past by the Grandmaster, paradoxically creating Camelot.[963]

To combat the actions of Kang, the Avengers shared their accomplishments as heroes while exposing their enemy as an immoral individual. This allowed the Avengers to gain access to the Missing Moment, the holy grail of existence.[621] However, the reboot of the Multiverse had been initiated by Kang and could not be stopped. In coalition, the Avengers and the Twilight Court were able to prepare the Missing Moment to be removed from existence and protect reality. The Impossible City played a last trick to prevent the sacrifice of its enemies, by releasing the Ashen Combine and inciting them to escape to oblivion, out of time and space, to stop the threat.[964] Kang was incarcerated for his crimes in Kyln-2. The Impossible City took the Twilight Court to the stars to share the heroic ideals of Earth's Mightiest Heroes. In the end, Captain Marvel called for the dissolution of the Avengers and suggested a reformation of the team.[965]

Armageddon[]

The fall of Doctor Doom's empire represented a political instability. As the heir of his legacy, Val Richards deactivated his legion of Doombots, while Latveria was left unattended. General Thunderbolt Ross foresaw a crisis and proposed an intervention.[966] He contacted Steve Rogers, the original Captain America for support. Instead, the star-spangled hero joined Nick Fury's new S.H.I.E.L.D., which put him into direct conflict against Ross, the Red Hulk. The situation ended up with Captain America being incapacitated, while the Red Hulk ascended to power in the ruins of Latveria, turning it into New America.[967] Simultaneously, the growing interest for weaponizing the Super-Soldier Program[968] led the Red Hulk to create an army of behemoth soldiers. In this setting, the Avengers reassembled, being joined by the Fantastic Four, Bucky, Namor, Spider-Man, and Wolverine in opposing the Red Hulk as he made a move to colonize Symkaria. David Colton, a rogue result of the Super-Soldier Program, joined the Avengers on probationary status since his main interest was to decommission any attempt to replicate the process that had empowered him and Rogers. Refusing to submit to recommendations from the United Nations to stand down, the Avengers assembled to fight for liberty.[969]

Trivia

  • The first time the famous Avengers' catchphrase "Avengers Assemble" was said was in Avengers #10 by Thor and has mostly appeared in Marvel media ever since.
  • In-universe, the comic-publishing company Marvel Comics made an arrangement with the Maria Stark Foundation to depict authorized adventures of the Avengers. Unlike the agreement made with the Fantastic Four, the Avengers didn't personally handle the arrangements for their series. Since the approvals and information flow were handled by Maria Stark Foundation intermediaries, Marvel's writers were given less details about the Avengers' exploits than the Fantastic Four. Because of this, Stan Lee once referred to Marvel's Avengers comics as "only 69% authorized."[970]
    • Additionally, since members of the Avengers maintained secret identities, Marvel was eventually given consent by the Maria Stark Foundation to create fictitious backstories for them. Before that, Stan Lee simply tried to focus solely on the team members in their costumed personas.[970]
  • The Avengers were parodied by DC Comics in the Superman/Batman series in the storyline "With a Vengeance!", where the Dark Knight and Man of Steel faced heroes created by Mr. Mxyzptlk and the Joker called the Maximums, who were comprised of Soldier (a patriotic hero, expy of Captain America), Viking (a nordic God, expy of Thor), Hornet (a half-human half-insect flying heroine, expy of Wasp), Skyscraper (a giant man in love with Hornet, expy of Giant-Man), Robot (a conscious robot in a bulky iron-suit, expy of Iron Man), Bowman (an archer, expy of Hawkeye), Wolfen (a bestial wolfman with tiger stripes, expy of Wolverine), Bug (a blue and red four-armed man, expy of Spider-Man) and Monster (a big creature with super-strength and ripped pants whose alter ego is weaker, expy of Hulk).
  • The Avengers were created because of a hold-up in the production of Daredevil #1, due to penciler Bill Everett being delayed. At the time, print time was booked ahead of time, and if the issue to be printed wasn't ready, the print time was still going to be charged. Because of this, Stan Lee created the Avengers, a group of already-established heroes, so it wouldn't take long to produce an issue featuring them.[971]
  • The Avengers and their comic book series share their name with the long-running British television series The Avengers which debuted in 1961, three years before the super hero team. Due to the popularity of both properties in their respective countries, their shared name has caused complications on both sides of the Atlantic ever since:
    • The Marvel comic has had to be retitled Avengers Assemble on several occasions for UK publication.
    • For North American publication, comics based upon the TV series have had to be retitled, usually a variant of Steed and Peel or Steed and Mrs. Peel.
    • The issues over the name don't appear to have been repeated with New Avengers, a title shared by both a later series in the Marvel franchise, and a revival of the TV series that aired in the 1970s.
